MGT 409 · Final Project · Kristine Feng

Throughline

Your weekly step-back: five minutes to see the bigger picture of your life, in your own words.

Throughline brings the pieces of your life together: your moments, photos, ideas and goals. The AI finds the threads that connect them to what matters to you and opens with a question, so you never start from a blank page. It's a team effort: the AI does the connecting, and you do the reflecting.

The problem we're solving

Life gets busy, and most of us are just trying to get through the day. We take photos we never look at again, write journal entries we never reread, and set goals in apps that only add to the to-do list. Each piece lives in its own silo, and nothing connects them. So we rarely lift our heads to see the bigger picture, and we end up feeling overwhelmed, lost, or unsure what it's all for.

How might we give people intentional space to step back and connect the pieces of their lives?

What's new

It shows its evidence. You shape the story.

What other apps already do
  • AI patterns across entries: Rosebud, Day One, Mindsera, Stoic
  • Links back to entries: Rosebud, Day One
  • Remembering feedback: Rosebud, ChatGPT memory
  • Photo resurfacing: Apple and Google Photos
What makes Throughline different
  • It shows its evidence: every observation quotes your own words, checked by code
  • It's built around you: your own values and goals, not a personality the AI guesses
  • It learns from you: tell it what fits and what doesn't, and it adjusts
  • You set the direction: nothing about your goals changes without your OK
  • No streaks or scores: a mirror, not a coach

None of the seven apps I reviewed offers all five together, based on their public product pages and help docs.

How the agents work

Three agents, four checks in plain code

Demo · Maya's weekly step-back

“This week”: her latest week, seen against three months of moments. Every quote is verified against its entry, for $0.0014.

Prompt examples to reflect on
“You've said meditation matters to you, but it hasn't come up in a while. Is it still something you want to make time for?”
“You've written that you struggle to face challenges, yet look at what you've handled this year…” followed by your own moments, quoted.
Demo · Reflect Back

You shape the story.

  • Adjust it: say “partly” or “not me” in your own words, and the Mirror listens and adjusts
  • Set the direction: it may suggest a change to your North Star, and nothing changes until you accept
  • It remembers: on the next Zoom Out, the Pattern Finder reads what you said
Cost to run · measured, gpt-6-luna

About a penny per person per month

$0.0012
per weekly Zoom Out ($0.0018 with search)
~1¢
per user per month
$97
per month for 10,000 users
Cut cost: photos read once and shrunk (−36% tokens, same description); stable prompt first (cached at 1/10 price); caps of $0.05 per run and $1 per day.
Surprise: for small journals, reading everything was 35% cheaper than agentic search (87% cached) and cited 9 vs 5 moments. So I added a router.
Safety · built and tested

Four risks, each with a defense that's been tested

  • Injection: the scanner holds it back, entries reach the model only as escaped data, and tools are read-only. In a live attack with the scanner off, the provider blocked the blatant one and the model ignored the subtle one.
  • Invented memories: code verifies every quote against its entry.
  • Crisis: resources (988), never AI analysis, and Zoom Out pauses.
  • Spend: caps per run, per day and per agent.

16 automated tests + a live attack test against gpt-6-luna
